Bootstrap a Network Estimate

Source: R/bootstrap_network.R
bootstrap_network.Rd

bootstrap_network() resamples the cases a network was estimated from, re-estimates the network on every resample with the same method and settings, and reports for each edge its bootstrap mean, standard deviation, confidence interval and a p-value, together with the network pruned to the edges that pass. It reads any network from build_network(), built-in method or registered estimator, as well as a netobject_group or mcml (every network is bootstrapped) and a wtna_mixed (both of its components). The cases are the sequences of a transition network (for one-hot data, its actors or sessions) and the rows of the data otherwise; with actor, whole actors are resampled (see Nested data and actor).

The p-value comes from one of two tests. With inference = "stability" it counts the replicates that fall outside a consistency range around the original weight (by default 75% to 125% of it), so a significant edge is one whose weight the resamples reproduce within that range. With inference = "threshold" it counts the replicates whose absolute weight falls below edge_threshold, so a significant edge stays above that threshold. In both, the p-value is that count plus one, divided by the number of replicates plus one, so it is never 0. Edges with a p-value below ci_level are kept in the pruned network.

The p-value counts replicates, so it cannot fall below 1 / (iter + 1): with too few iterations no edge can pass a small ci_level. The stability test asks whether a weight is reproduced within a range, not whether it differs from zero, and because the range is a proportion of the weight, a weak edge has to be reproduced within a narrow band; read the interval beside the test. The bootstrap describes how the estimate varies over resamples of one sample; to compare groups, use permutation().

Usage

bootstrap_network(
  x,
  iter = 1000L,
  ci_level = 0.05,
  inference = "stability",
  consistency_range = c(0.75, 1.25),
  edge_threshold = NULL,
  seed = NULL,
  boundary = c("inclusive", "strict"),
  ci_method = c("percentile", "basic"),
  actor = NULL
)

# S3 method for class 'net_bootstrap'
print(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'net_bootstrap'
summary(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'net_bootstrap_group'
print(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'net_bootstrap_group'
summary(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'wtna_boot_mixed'
print(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'wtna_boot_mixed'
summary(object, ...)

Arguments

x

The network: a netobject that carries its data (any network from build_network()), or a cograph_network, which is converted first. A netobject_group or mcml bootstraps every network it holds (for an mcml, the macro network and each cluster's), and a wtna_mixed bootstraps both of its components (see Value). A network without its data raises an error, and one that rests on a single sequence, or one-hot data with no actor or session, has nothing to resample and raises an error of class nestimate_single_sequence. For the print() methods: the result of bootstrap_network().

iter

The number of bootstrap replicates, at least 2. Default 1000.

ci_level

The significance level, between 0 and 1: the confidence intervals cover 1 - ci_level, and an edge is significant when its p-value is below ci_level. Default 0.05.

inference

The test behind the p-values. "stability" (default) counts the replicates outside the consistency range around the original weight; "threshold" counts the replicates whose absolute weight is below edge_threshold.

consistency_range

For inference = "stability": the two multipliers of the original weight that bound the consistency range. Default c(0.75, 1.25). For a negative weight the bounds are swapped, so the range still runs from the lower to the upper value. Not used by "threshold".

edge_threshold

For inference = "threshold": the absolute weight a replicate must reach. Default NULL, the 10th percentile of the non-zero absolute original weights. Not used by "stability".

seed

A number that makes the resamples reproducible. The session's own random stream is left as it was. For a netobject_group or mcml, each network is bootstrapped from the same seed; for a wtna_mixed, the seed is set once, before both components. Default NULL.

boundary

For inference = "stability": how a replicate that lands exactly on a bound of the consistency range counts. "inclusive" (default, as in tna) counts it as outside (\(\le\) / \(\ge\)); "strict" counts only replicates strictly outside (\(<\) / \(>\)).

ci_method

The confidence interval for the edge weights. "percentile" (default) uses the empirical bootstrap quantiles (Efron). "basic" reflects those quantiles around the observed weight, \((2\hat{\theta} - q_{1-\alpha/2}, 2\hat{\theta} - q_{\alpha/2})\) (Davison & Hinkley 1997, eq. 5.6), which corrects first-order bootstrap bias but can give bounds outside the natural weight range near its limits (for example below 0 for a transition probability close to 0).

actor

The column identifying the actor each sequence belongs to (for example "student_id" for sessions nested in students, "Group" for students nested in teams), looked up in the network's metadata or its wide sequence data. With it, whole actors are resampled; see Nested data and actor. Default NULL: sequences are resampled one by one. It is available for sequence-based transition networks ("relative", "frequency", "co_occurrence"); a method outside the fast path (see Details) raises an error of class nestimate_actor_unsupported. A value that is not a single column name, or that names fewer than two actors, raises an error of class nestimate_bad_actor; a column that is absent or has missing values, one of class nestimate_actor_missing; and ids that do not give one actor per sequence, one of class nestimate_actor_misaligned.

...

For the print() and summary() methods: ignored.

object

For the summary() methods: the result of bootstrap_network().

Value

A net_bootstrap object. print() lists the five strongest significant edges (by absolute bootstrap mean, with their interval) and reports the iterations, the number of significant edges, the interval level and the test, and with actor the ICC and design effect; summary() returns one row per edge of the original network; cograph::splot() draws the bootstrapped network; net_prune() with method = "bootstrap" removes the non-significant edges from the original network. The fields:

original

The original netobject.

mean, sd

The bootstrap mean and standard deviation of each weight, as matrices.

p_values

The matrix of p-values.

significant

The original weights where the p-value is below ci_level, and 0 elsewhere, self-loops included.

ci_lower, ci_upper

The matrices of interval bounds.

cr_lower, cr_upper

The matrices of consistency-range bounds (used by "stability" only).

summary

A data frame with one row per non-zero original edge (one row per unordered pair in an undirected network) and the columns from, to, weight, mean, sd, p_value, sig, ci_lower and ci_upper, plus cr_lower and cr_upper with inference = "stability".

model

The pruned netobject, whose weights are significant: its non-significant edges, self-loops included, are zero. (The network net_prune() returns keeps every self-loop.)

method, params, iter, ci_level, inference, ci_method

The bootstrap settings.

consistency_range, edge_threshold

The test settings.

actor, n_actors

The actor column and its number of actors; NULL without actor.

clustering

Only with actor: a one-row data frame of n_sequences, n_actors, icc, icc_ci_lower, icc_ci_upper and deff_edges.

clustering_edges

Only with actor: one row per edge of summary, with from, to, icc, sd_actor, sd_sequence and deff.

A netobject_group or mcml gives a net_bootstrap_group, a named list of net_bootstrap results: its print() reports each network's significant and total edges and the significant edges all networks share (when the networks have edges in common); its summary() is described with the methods below. A wtna_mixed gives a wtna_boot_mixed holding the transition and cooccurrence results.

The print() methods return their input invisibly. The summary() method of a net_bootstrap returns its per-edge table, the summary field described above. For a net_bootstrap_group it stacks those tables into one data frame, with a first column group naming the network each row comes from; for a wtna_boot_mixed it returns a list of the transition and cooccurrence tables.

Details

The two tests and the inclusive boundary rule follow tna::bootstrap().

Transition networks ("relative", "frequency", "co_occurrence", and wtna networks, which hold the same one-hot counts) take a fast path: the count matrix of every sequence is computed once, and each replicate sums the counts of the sequences drawn, then applies the network's normalisation, scaling and threshold. With params = list(concat = k), the consecutive groups of up to k rows merged by the estimator are the sequences resampled; joins inside each merged sequence are retained. With actor, a merged sequence must belong entirely to one actor. Every other method (the association methods, "attention", "ngram", "gap", "reverse" and registered estimators) is re-estimated in full on resampled rows. A replicate whose estimation fails, or that loses a node, is left out of the p-values without a warning, and the bootstrap statistics are computed over the remaining replicates; if every replicate fails, every p-value is 1.

A network built from an edge list (for example an mcml from build_mcml() with from and to) has no sequences, so each transition is resampled as an independent case, with a warning that points to the alternatives.

Nested data and actor

The bootstrap resamples sequences as independent units. When sequences are nested in actors (sessions in students, students in teams), actor names the column identifying the actor, and whole actors are resampled with replacement, keeping all their sequences together: the cluster bootstrap that resamples at the top level only (Davison & Hinkley, 1997, section 3.8; Field & Welsh, 2007). The number of sequences per replicate then varies with the actors drawn.

With actor, the result also reports the nesting effect. The ICC is the proportion of the total variance that lies between actors (Shrout & Fleiss, 1979); an ICC close to 0 indicates little evidence of a nesting effect. It is computed as in permutation. The design effect is the ratio of the variance under the nested design to the variance had the sequences been sampled independently (Kish, 1965): here, the variance of the edge weights over actor-level replicates divided by their variance over sequence-level replicates drawn in the same run, reported as the median over edges. actor is available for transition networks ("relative", "frequency", "co_occurrence").

References

Davison, A. C., & Hinkley, D. V. (1997). Bootstrap Methods and Their Application. Cambridge University Press.

Field, C. A., & Welsh, A. H. (2007). Bootstrapping clustered data. Journal of the Royal Statistical Society: Series B, 69(3), 369-390.

Kish, L. (1965). Survey Sampling. Wiley.

Shrout, P. E., & Fleiss, J. L. (1979). Intraclass correlations: Uses in assessing rater reliability. Psychological Bulletin, 86(2), 420-428.

See also

certainty for the closed-form Bayesian counterpart (same result layout, no resampling); build_network

Examples

net <- build_network(data.frame(V1 = c("A","B","C"), V2 = c("B","C","A")),
  method = "relative")
boot <- bootstrap_network(net, iter = 10)
# \donttest{
set.seed(1)
seqs <- data.frame(
  V1 = sample(LETTERS[1:4], 30, TRUE), V2 = sample(LETTERS[1:4], 30, TRUE),
  V3 = sample(LETTERS[1:4], 30, TRUE), V4 = sample(LETTERS[1:4], 30, TRUE)
)
net <- build_network(seqs, method = "relative")
boot <- bootstrap_network(net, iter = 100)
print(boot)

# Students nested in teams: resample whole teams
teams <- build_network(group_regulation_long, method = "relative",
                       actor = "Actor", action = "Action", time = "Time",
                       group = "Achiever")
bootstrap_network(teams, iter = 100, actor = "Group", seed = 1)
